methods.description: Identify the greatest and smallest complete data values and subtract minimum from maximum.
Count repeated complete values, report every tied most frequent value, and report no mode when every value appears once.
Add every data value, including repetitions, divide by the count, and round only as requested with an approximation sign.
Order the complete values and select the one middle score or average the two middle scores.
Use (n+1)/2 as the median position and interpret a half position as the mean of the adjacent ordered values.
Use the key to reconstruct every whole data value from its stem and leaf, retain repetitions and omit empty stems before calculating the requested statistics.
Read one value for each observation from its column height and the labelled value scale, then order or total these values for the requested statistics; the heights are not frequencies.
Use range=maximum-minimum to find an unknown extreme from the given range and the other extreme, and check it by subtraction.
For an explicitly ordered even-count list, make the two middle values total twice the given median, subtract the known middle value and check the order.
Use the given mean to obtain the total, the given median to identify the middle score, the mode to require repetition, and ascending order to place the remaining unknown values.

sourceReview.observation: Stage 4 explicitly teaches all four statistics for simple datasets and interpretation of data displays.
sourceReview.adjustments: Used the earliest Stage 4 scope; later Stage 6 membership is reuse only.

sourceReview.locator: Summary definitions; Range complete teaching, example, guided practice and Key Ideas
sourceReview.observation: Definitions distinguish spread from centre. Range is maximum minus minimum; the original example substitutes extrema before subtraction.
sourceReview.adjustments: Adapted simple positive whole-number lists. Retained all good baseline values. No decorative range diagram is necessary in a list example.

sourceReview.locator: Mode complete teaching, examples, Key Ideas and practice
sourceReview.observation: Sort and count actual values; preserve ties and no-mode cases. Repeated values in the new examples have the specific purpose of teaching mode.
sourceReview.adjustments: Source practice 2(d) says only 7 for 5,5,7,7,12; the correct tied modes are 5 and 7. Practice 4 says drive although walk occurs four times; these source answer errors are not imported.

sourceReview.locator: Mean complete teaching, example, guided practice and Key Ideas
sourceReview.observation: Use the total divided by the number of data values, showing substitution and total before division. Source example uses an approximation symbol for rounding.
sourceReview.adjustments: Adapted the original substitution procedure to manageable positive scores, with explicit one-decimal-place instructions for nonterminating means. No unknown-mean or frequency-table method is imported from the sibling skill.

sourceReview.locator: Median complete teaching, paired examples, guided practice and Key Ideas
sourceReview.observation: Sort in ascending order; odd counts have one middle value and even counts require the mean of two middle values. Viewed the actual image19 comparison.
sourceReview.adjustments: Adapted the paired odd/even teaching into two full-statistic examples; preserved baseline ordered-list medians and all valid values.

sourceReview.observation: Six cards have median 12; the actual source image24 has 7,20,30,14,9 and a missing card. The two middle values must average 12, giving missing value 10. This directly supports the retained narrow inverse-median tasks.
sourceReview.adjustments: New inverse-median example explicitly supplies ascending order and checks it after finding the missing value. No general equation-solving extension or new algebraic-expression dataset is introduced.

sourceReview.locator: Summary statistics from a list complete teaching, example and guided practice
sourceReview.observation: All four definitions and calculation procedures are combined in one worked dataset. The numerical working is original Stage 4 calculation teaching.
sourceReview.adjustments: Adapted source values to positive score lists, retaining all four complete requested calculations. Deliberately chose different mean/median/range/mode results unless equality is an explicit condition.

sourceReview.locator: Summary statistics complete reverse-range practice question 5
sourceReview.observation: Given range 17 and minimum 9, find maximum 26 by adding the range to the minimum.
sourceReview.adjustments: Retained the baseline reverse-range task and adapted one new example; the method follows the definition, rather than a new advanced statistical procedure.

sourceReview.locator: Summary statistics complete missing-data questions 11 and 12
sourceReview.observation: Original Stage 4 practice combines ordered data with mean, median, mode and range constraints and separately asks missing values for individual statistics. Supports the valid narrow mastery items.
sourceReview.adjustments: New five-value contrast uses mean for the total, median for the middle value, mode for a repeated value and ordering to decide its position. The stated equality of mean/median/mode is purposeful, not an accidental numerical coincidence.

sourceReview.locator: Median position complete teaching, paired examples, guided practice and first two practice questions
sourceReview.observation: Position=(n+1)/2 gives an ordinal location; half positions mean averaging adjacent scores, not reporting the position as the answer. Actual image38 inspected.
sourceReview.adjustments: New paired odd/even example keeps position and value distinct. Unneeded long, negative and large source practice datasets are not added to the current simple score assessment bank.

sourceReview.locator: Analysing stem-and-leaf plots complete example and guided practice
sourceReview.observation: The original worked plot includes repeated leaves and an empty stem, reads whole values using the key and calculates all four statistics, using median position for an even count.
sourceReview.adjustments: Adapted all source plot values while retaining repeated observations and an empty stem. Column-height interpretation is an honest adaptation of Stage 4 data-display scope and list calculation; no claim that this section contains a column-graph worked example.
